subject: Transport selection for private deployment: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN

Subject: Transport selection for private deployment: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN

Hi Sophia / BogotaTech networking team,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. We are starting to scope the private deployment for your production environment and need to lock the transport pattern so infra can size and prep the onboarding runbook. High level options we see:

- VPC Peering (account-to-account peering) — lower latency, simple routing, but requires peering across accounts and may collide with your org security boundaries.
- AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints / ENIs) — strong isolation, explicit endpoint governance, easier to restrict flows; potential egress path and IP management considerations.
- Site-to-site VPN (IPSec) — easiest for multi-cloud/on-prem compatibility and quick pilot, higher latency and operational overhead for scale.

Could you confirm the following so we can recommend a primary pattern and a fallback?
1) Any organizational block on cross-account peering or a requirement that all network flows go through PrivateLink endpoints?
2) Expected sustained TPS / tokens-per-second for production inference (so we can validate throughput on PLINK vs peering).
3) Any static IP allowlisting requirement (we can provide egress IP ranges) and whether your security team prefers ENI-based endpoints or dedicated ALB fronting.

I attached a short XLS with our initial requirements and the constraints we tested in sandbox. Once you confirm constraints we’ll produce a short recommendation doc and propose a meeting to finalize.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Transport selection for private deployment: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN

Hi Aisha — thanks for the summary and the XLS. Quick answers from our side:

1) We have a strict multi-account policy that discourages long-lived VPC peering across business unit accounts. Peering is allowed for short-term projects but requires a formal change control and network review.
2) Production expected steady-state: ~150 requests/sec at 1.2k tokens/request average during peak windows. Burst to 350 req/s for short periods.
3) We will need static egress IPs to be allow-listed with our perimeter firewall. Our security team prefers interface endpoints (ENIs) or PrivateLink where flows are ingress-only to our VPC; they are wary of open peering routes.

We attached our internal network policy that outlines the controls. Given that, PrivateLink looks most compatible from a policy standpoint. However, we need clarification on planned egress flows from Redwood (for callbacks, telemetry) and how you manage HA across AZs.

Can you provide estimated latency ranges (p50/p99) for each pattern at the throughput above and a short plan for failover (PrivateLink fallback to S2S until PrivateLink is fully provisioned)?

Best regards,
Sophia Lawrence
Head of Infrastructure | BogotaTech
[Attachment: bt-network-policy.pdf (application/pdf)]

Sophia / team — thanks for the clarity. Short technical responses below and a recommended approach.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Primary: AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoint) for production — aligns with your multi-account policy and security preference for explicit ingress-only endpoints.
- Fallback for dev/staging: S2S VPN as a temporary onboarding option while PrivateLink endpoints are provisioned.
- VPC Peering: Operationally simpler for pure single-account setups, but because you have the multi-account restriction and want strict routing controls, it’s lower priority.

Performance guidance (approx):
- VPC Peering: p50 ~ 8–12 ms, p99 ~ 25–40 ms (within same region, no proxy). Scales well for sustained throughput but requires route table management.
- PrivateLink (ENI-based): p50 ~ 12–18 ms, p99 ~ 30–60 ms depending on AZ mapping and cross-AZ hops. Throughput is generally fine for your numbers; we’ve validated sustained 500 req/s with tuned connection pooling from our side.
- S2S VPN: p50 ~ 35–60 ms, p99 ~ 100–180 ms depending on gateway and encryption overhead; good for short-term or if you need on-prem connectivity.

Operational notes:
- IP allowlisting — we can provide a small set of static egress IPs for management/telemetry, and we will front production PrivateLink with dedicated interface endpoints in each AZ to avoid cross-AZ transits as much as possible.
- HA/failover — our standard is multi-AZ endpoints + health checks and a documented runbook to fail traffic to a peered fallback / VPN in case the endpoint provisioning is delayed.

Attached is a short CSV with latency/throughput examples from similar customers (not identical load but representative). Happy to run a small smoke test from your staging to validate numbers.

I’ll join the call if you want to go through diagrams and failover steps.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: plink-vs-peering-latency-table.csv (text/csv)]
